security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, example URLs, and abbreviated URL placeholders. Confirmed risks include RunComfy CLI execution, global CLI installation, third-party API processing, output downloads, and login side effects. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: External CLI execution and global installation are required.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend a pinned RunComfy CLI version, verify the package source, and ask users to confirm before running install or edit commands.

remediation.issue: Prompts and image URL references are processed by RunComfy.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short privacy warning before examples and advise users not to send confidential assets without approval.

remediation.issue: RunComfy login stores an API token in the user config directory.
remediation.suggestion: Document token revocation, avoid logging token values, and prefer RUNCOMFY_TOKEN in controlled CI environments.

content.user_title: Edit Images with Nano Banana on RunComfy
content.value_statement: Image editing prompts often drift from the intended subject, framing, or brand style. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured guidance for RunComfy Nano Banana edits.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Nano Banana Edit instead of GPT Image 2 edit, Flux Kontext, or text-to-image generation.
Provides the RunComfy endpoint name and input fields for image-to-image edits.
Shows single-image, batch, and targeted spatial edit invocation patterns.
Guides prompts that preserve identity, pose, clothing, framing, and brand details.
Documents batch controls such as aspect ratio, resolution, seed, and output count.
Summarizes RunComfy CLI exit codes, token storage, outbound endpoints, and output behavior.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and valid authentication.
Requires publicly reachable HTTPS image URLs for input images.
Does not perform edits locally; prompts and image references are processed by RunComfy.
Long compound edit prompts can cause model drift and should be split into smaller passes.

use_cases.title: Create Product Gallery Variants
use_cases.description: Edit many product images with consistent framing, background style, and resolution settings.

use_cases.title: Refresh Ad Creative
use_cases.description: Generate controlled background, layout, or copy variants while preserving the main subject.

use_cases.title: Localize Visual Assets
use_cases.description: Replace specific labels, backgrounds, or visible details while keeping the rest of the image stable.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Background Swap
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana Edit on this image URL. Keep the subject identity, pose, clothing, and framing unchanged. Replace only the background with a clean studio setting.

prompt_templates.title: Target One Area
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana Edit. Keep the full composition unchanged except for the upper-right sign. Replace the sign text with the requested phrase in the same style.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Product Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana Edit for these product image URLs. Apply the same background, aspect ratio, resolution, and prompt structure to every image for gallery consistency.

prompt_templates.title: Two-Pass Refinement Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a two-pass Nano Banana Edit workflow. First preserve identity while changing the background. Then adjust only the clothing color without changing pose or face.

output_examples.input: A portrait needs a new rainy city background while the person must remain recognizable.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects Nano Banana Edit, keeps identity and pose first in the prompt, and requests only a background change.

output_examples.input: A product team needs the same object edited across several catalog images.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends a batch edit, locked aspect ratio, fixed resolution, and consistent wording for every image.

output_examples.input: A designer wants to remove only one object from the left side of a still life image.
output_examples.output: The assistant writes a spatially scoped edit that removes the left object and preserves the remaining objects, table, and lighting.

best_practices: Start prompts with what must stay unchanged, then state the exact edit.
Use precise spatial language for local edits, such as background only or upper-right corner.
Lock aspect ratio and resolution when editing a related batch of images.
anti_patterns: Do not combine many unrelated edits in one prompt when visual stability matters.
Do not use vague instructions such as make it better or more premium.
Do not send confidential image URLs unless RunComfy processing is approved.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides Nano Banana 2 image-to-image edits through the RunComfy CLI.

faq.question: Does it edit images locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the RunComfy model API through the local RunComfy CLI.

faq.question: How many input images can it describe for one call?
faq.answer: The documented endpoint accepts 1 to 20 input image URLs per call.

faq.question: When should I use another model?
faq.answer: Use GPT Image 2 edit for stronger multilingual in-image text edits, and text-to-image generation for new images.

faq.question: What authentication is required?
faq.answer: The RunComfy CLI must be installed and authenticated with login or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN value.

faq.question: What privacy boundary should users know?
faq.answer: Prompts and image URL references are sent to RunComfy, so confidential assets need prior approval.
